above_floor: above the turntable floor of the profile
track_estimated: · not every gap found, some boundaries estimated
track_col_clicks_title: Clicks and pops per minute, without crackle
track_col_confirmed_title: Share of clicks confirmed by the grooveclean network
track_hint: Per track: clicks without crackle per minute, the worst in red. Gaps between tracks do not count here; they are in “Clicks quiet”.
tech_balance_value: Bass {bass} · low mids {low_mid} · mids {mid} · presence {presence} · treble {treble} dB
tech_peak_help: Highest sample value per channel. Above −1 dBFS it gets tight, 0 dBFS = clipped.
tech_true_peak_help: Peak of the reconstructed signal (4× oversampled, ITU-R BS.1770). Can exceed 0 dBTP even though no sample clips.
tech_rms_help: Average power of the whole groove per channel.
tech_crest_help: Peak minus RMS: the dynamics. Vinyl is typically 14–20 dB, heavily compressed pressings below 12 dB.
tech_loudness_help: ITU-R BS.1770-4 with K-weighting and gating, as in WaveLab/RX. For reference against the digital master or between pressings.
tech_dc_help: DC component of the signal. Above 0.5 % it points to the recording chain (coupling capacitor, converter).
tech_correlation_help: Median L/R cross-correlation in music blocks: 1 = mono, 0 = uncorrelated, negative = out of phase (vinyl cutting avoids this, the stylus would jump).
tech_width_help: Side (L−R) relative to mid (L+R) in the music. −∞ = mono; above 0 dB would be more side than mid, unusual on vinyl.
tech_balance_help: Share of each band in the total power (20 Hz–20 kHz), in dB. For comparing two pressings or before/after.
tech_centroid_help: Power-weighted mean frequency of the music: higher = brighter.
tech_rumble_help: 20–100 Hz without the 50/100 Hz lines, in quiet passages. Reflects drive and placement (record warps lie below this range).
tech_hum_help: Lines at 50 and 100 Hz in quiet passages; more than 10 dB above the surroundings = clear hum (ground, power supplies).
tech_noise_value: {db} dBFS · A-weighted {a} dBFS · {rel} dB relative to the music
tech_noise_help: Level of the quiet passages. Relative to the music it counts towards the grade; live albums (audience) fail here.
tech_chain_help: Self-noise of the recording chain with the stylus up (calibration). Whatever the groove adds on top is record and turntable.

tech_clip_groove.one: {n} sample in the groove, first at {t}
tech_clip_groove.other: {n} samples in the groove, first at {t}

tech_clip_help: Samples at full scale. Harmless at stylus drop; in the groove it makes the comparison useless.
tech_level_value: music {db} dB relative to the reference tone ({ref} dBFS)
tech_level_help: Music level relative to the 1 kHz reference tone of the turntable profile (5 cm/s). Normally 0 to −10 dB; well below that the gain is off, and the detector misses small clicks.
tech_speed_help: From the turntable profile; skip detection looks for the true revolution period.
tech_events_value: {pop} pops · {click} clicks · {tick} crackle · quiet {quiet}, music {music}, excluded {excluded}
tech_events_help: Detected defects by type and region (excluded = before stylus drop / after lift).
tech_recording_help: Duration, detected groove (stylus down), format and recording device.

weak.one: {n} weak match not counted (similarity below 0.40 or period not exactly one revolution): usually the rhythm of the music, not a skip.
weak.other: {n} weak matches not counted (similarity below 0.40 or period not exactly one revolution): usually the rhythm of the music, not a skip.

none: No backward skips counted{end}. Forward skips only show up when two recordings are compared.
jumped_back: The stylus jumped back {n}×: one revolution repeats. The skips are in the list below: listen and judge them (run-out groove or no skip). If the skips were at a different place in every recording, it is the setup (turntable check); at the same place, it is more likely the record.
